Field snapshots that were not modified in that particular edit are returned as null. For example, if an edit only changed the title, the description, start_date, and due_date fields will all be null. The title field is always populated because every todo is required to have a title per business rules.

Edit history entries are immutable — once created, they cannot be modified or individually deleted. The only removal path is cascade deletion when the parent todo is permanently deleted from the trash.
ITodoAppEditHistory.ISummary.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from todo_app_edit_histories table. Columns mapped: id, title, description, start_date, due_date, created_at. Excluded: todo_app_todo_id (parent todo known from the URL path parameter {todoId} in the edit-histories endpoint), todo relation (parent context unnecessary in summary view), updated_at (immutable record — edit history entries are never modified after creation, so updated_at always equals created_at). Nullable columns (description, start_date, due_date) use oneOf with null — they are always present in the response body but null when that specific field was not changed in the edit represented by this entry. Title is always non-null per business rules (every todo requires a title).

fingerprint.description:
Device fingerprint hash uniquely identifying the guest visitor.

A hashed representation of the visitor's device characteristics, used to recognize returning unauthenticated visitors across visits. The system performs an upsert lookup by this value — if a matching guest identity exists, it is reused; otherwise, a new guest record is created.

This field is required and must be a non-empty string.
fingerprint.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from todo_app_guests.fingerprint. Unique constraint — used as lookup key for upsert: find existing guest by fingerprint or create new guest identity. Must be a non-empty string.

href.description:
Current page URL where the guest initiated the join flow.

Captures the full URL of the page the visitor was on when triggering the join. This metadata is stored in the guest session record for security auditing and context tracking.

This field is required — the client must always provide the current page URL to ensure complete session audit trails.
href.x-autobe-specification: Stored in todo_app_guest_sessions.href. Captures the full URL of the page where the guest initiated the join flow. Required per IJoin session context rules — the client must always provide the current page URL. Format: uri.

referrer.description:
Referring page URL that led the guest to the current page.

Captures the HTTP Referer header value indicating where the visitor came from before arriving at the join page. This metadata is stored in the guest session record for security auditing and traffic source analysis.

This field is required — the client must always provide the referring page URL to ensure complete session audit trails.
referrer.x-autobe-specification: Stored in todo_app_guest_sessions.referrer. Captures the HTTP Referer header value indicating where the visitor came from. Required per IJoin session context rules — the client must always provide the referring page URL. Format: uri.

ITodoAppGuest.IJoin.description:
Guest join request containing the device fingerprint hash and optional session context metadata.

The fingerprint is a hashed representation of device characteristics used to uniquely identify returning unauthenticated visitors across visits. It serves as the primary lookup key — if a guest with the same fingerprint already exists, their identity record is reused; otherwise, a new guest identity is created.

Session context fields capture the page where the guest initiated the join flow. The href records the current page URL, while the referrer captures the referring page that led the guest there. Both fields are optional; when omitted, they default to an empty string server-side. The guest's IP address is captured automatically from the incoming request and is not part of the request body.

This endpoint is the entry point for unauthenticated visitors. Upon success, the server returns a JWT access token and refresh token pair scoped to the guest identity and newly created session.
ITodoAppGuest.IJoin.x-autobe-specification: Maps: fingerprint → todo_app_guests.fingerprint (unique constraint, used for upsert lookup — find existing guest or create new). Session context: href → todo_app_guest_sessions.href, referrer → todo_app_guest_sessions.referrer (both optional; when omitted by client, server defaults to empty string). ip is captured server-side from X-Forwarded-For header or remote address — never accepted from client. Excluded from request body: id (auto-generated UUID), created_at and updated_at (system-managed timestamps), sessions (server-side session creation during join flow).

id.description:
Unique identifier of the authenticated guest.

A UUID v4 string that uniquely identifies the guest identity record in `todo_app_guests`. This identifier is embedded as the `sub` (subject) claim within both JWT tokens, binding the tokens to this specific guest. The same guest retains this identifier across multiple sessions and token refresh cycles.
id.x-autobe-specification: Sourced from `todo_app_guests.id`. UUID primary key of the guest identity record. This value is also embedded as the `sub` (subject) claim within both the access and refresh JWT tokens, cryptographically binding the tokens to this specific guest identity.

fingerprint.description:
Device fingerprint hash uniquely identifying the guest visitor.

A hashed representation of the visitor's device characteristics, used to recognize returning unauthenticated visitors across visits. This value is unique across all guest records in `todo_app_guests`. The fingerprint persists across sessions — the same device always resolves to the same guest identity when calling the join endpoint.
fingerprint.x-autobe-specification: Sourced from `todo_app_guests.fingerprint`. Unique device fingerprint hash looked up or created during the join operation via the unique fingerprint index. Used to recognize returning unauthenticated visitors across visits without requiring persistent cookies or credentials.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the guest identity was first recorded.

ISO 8601 formatted date-time indicating the moment this guest first visited the application and their identity was created in `todo_app_guests`. This timestamp remains unchanged across subsequent visits and token refresh cycles.
created_at.x-autobe-specification: Sourced from `todo_app_guests.created_at`. Timestamp set once when the guest identity is first inserted into `todo_app_guests`. Never updated on subsequent join operations. Represents the first time this guest visited the application.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the guest identity record was last updated.

ISO 8601 formatted date-time reflecting the most recent activity associated with this guest identity. This value is updated on each join operation, serving as a last-seen indicator. It does not change during token refresh operations — only the join endpoint triggers an update.
updated_at.x-autobe-specification: Sourced from `todo_app_guests.updated_at`. Updated to now() on each join operation, even when the guest identity already exists. Serves as a last-seen indicator — reflects the most recent time this guest interacted with the join endpoint. Not updated during refresh operations.

token.x-autobe-specification: Authorization token comes from the session table.

ITodoAppGuest.IAuthorized.description:
JWT token pair issued to an authenticated guest, together with the guest's identity information.

Returned after a successful guest join or token refresh operation. Contains the guest's unique identifier and device fingerprint alongside a JWT access token and refresh token pair. Both tokens are cryptographically scoped to the guest identity and the specific session created during authentication.

**Token Usage**: The access token is short-lived and must be included in the Authorization header (Bearer scheme) for all authenticated API calls. The refresh token has a longer lifetime and can be exchanged for a new token pair via the refresh endpoint without re-submitting the device fingerprint.

**Identity Fields**: The id, fingerprint, created_at, and updated_at fields reflect the persistent guest identity record in `todo_app_guests`. These remain consistent across multiple sessions and token refresh cycles.

**Session Independence**: Each join or refresh call creates a new session record in `todo_app_guest_sessions`; the returned tokens are scoped to that specific session. Guest tokens grant access only to guest-permitted endpoints and cannot access member-only resources such as todos, trash, edit history, or user profiles.
ITodoAppGuest.IAuthorized.x-autobe-specification: Computed authorization response assembled at the service layer. Guest identity fields (id, fingerprint, created_at, updated_at) are sourced from the `todo_app_guests` record looked up or created during the join operation. The token pair is generated entirely server-side: access token (short-lived JWT, ~15 minutes) with claims sub=guest_id, session_id, kind="guest"; refresh token (long-lived JWT, ~7 days) with additional claim type="refresh". token.expired_at is derived from the access TTL (now + access TTL). token.refreshable_until is derived from the refresh TTL (now + refresh TTL). Both tokens are cryptographically signed. Used as the response body for POST /todoApp/auth/guest/join and POST /todoApp/auth/guest/refresh.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the todo.

A UUID v4 value assigned by the server when the todo is created. This identifier is immutable and serves as the primary key for all todo operations — retrieving, updating, toggling completion status, soft-deleting, restoring, and permanently deleting.
id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from todo_app_todos.id. UUID v4 primary key auto-generated by the server on todo creation. Immutable after creation.

title.description:
Short text describing the task.

The title is the only required field when creating a todo. It must contain meaningful, non-whitespace text. The title can be edited at any time, and each change is recorded in the todo's edit history.
title.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from todo_app_todos.title. NOT NULL column — must be non-empty and not whitespace-only. Validated at the service layer on both create and update.

description.description:
Longer text providing additional detail about the task.

This field is optional — it may be null when no description has been provided. Passing null clears any previously set description. Each change to the description is recorded in the todo's edit history.
description.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from todo_app_todos.description. Nullable column — accepts null or empty string to clear. No length limit enforced at the database level.

start_date.description:
The date and time when work on the task is intended to begin.

Optional — may be null when no start date has been set. When both a start date and a due date are provided, the due date must not be earlier than the start date. Passing null clears any previously set start date. Changes are recorded in the todo's edit history.
start_date.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from todo_app_todos.start_date. Nullable timestamptz column. When both start_date and due_date are non-null, the service layer validates that due_date is not earlier than start_date.

due_date.description:
The date and time by which the task should be completed.

Optional — may be null when no due date has been set. When both a start date and a due date are provided, the due date must not be earlier than the start date. Passing null clears any previously set due date. Changes are recorded in the todo's edit history.
due_date.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from todo_app_todos.due_date. Nullable timestamptz column. When both start_date and due_date are non-null, the service layer validates that due_date is not earlier than start_date.

completed_at.description:
Indicates whether the todo is complete and when it was marked so.

When null, the todo is incomplete. When set to a timestamp, the todo is complete and the value records the exact date and time completion was toggled. The completion status can be toggled freely between incomplete and complete any number of times. Toggling to complete sets this to the current timestamp; toggling back to incomplete clears it to null.
completed_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from todo_app_todos.completed_at. Nullable timestamptz column. NULL means incomplete; a non-NULL timestamp means complete and records the exact time the todo was marked complete. Toggled via the dedicated toggle endpoint — not set directly on create or update.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the todo was first created.

Set automatically by the server at creation time and never changes. This value can be used to sort todos chronologically — newest first or oldest first.
created_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from todo_app_todos.created_at. NOT NULL timestamptz column. Auto-generated by the server on insert — never set by the client. Immutable after creation.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp of the most recent modification to the todo.

Updated automatically by the server whenever any attribute changes — including title, description, start date, due date edits, completion status toggles, soft-deletion, and restoration from trash. This reflects the last change of any kind to the todo record.
updated_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from todo_app_todos.updated_at. NOT NULL timestamptz column. Auto-updated by the server on any attribute change including title/description/date edits, completion toggles, soft-delete, and restore operations.

ITodoAppTodo.description:
A single todo item with all its details.

Represents an individual task owned by the authenticated member. Each todo has a required title, an optional description, optional start and due dates, and a completion status tracked via the completed_at timestamp. When completed_at is null, the todo is incomplete; when set, it records the exact time the todo was marked complete.

Todos are completely private — each member can only access their own todos. Only active (non-trashed) todos appear through this schema; soft-deleted todos in the trash are accessible through dedicated trash browsing endpoints. Every attribute change updates the updated_at timestamp automatically.
ITodoAppTodo.x-autobe-specification: Direct column mapping from todo_app_todos table for active (non-trashed) todos filtered by deleted_at IS NULL. id: UUID PK auto-generated on insert. title: NOT NULL, non-empty. description, start_date, due_date: nullable, accept null. completed_at: nullable timestamptz — NULL means incomplete, non-NULL timestamp means complete. created_at: NOT NULL, auto-generated on insert. updated_at: NOT NULL, auto-updated on any change. Excluded: member_id (implicit from authenticated JWT session), deleted_at (active-only context — all operations using this type filter deleted_at IS NULL), member relation (authenticated user, no nested objects), editHistories relation (browsed separately via dedicated endpoint). No JOINs, no nested objects.

instruction:
Test the following scenarios for the Multi-User Todo Application:

- User signup with valid email and password
- User signup with invalid email (duplicate, malformed)
- User login with correct credentials
- User login with incorrect password
- User change password
- User delete account (verify all todos and trash are permanently deleted)
- Edit display name on profile

- Create a todo with title only (verify it defaults to incomplete)
- Create a todo with all fields (title, description, start date, due date)
- Create a todo without title (should fail)
- View paginated todo list
- View a single todo with all details
- Toggle todo completion status (complete → incomplete → complete)
- Edit todo fields (verify edit history is created)
- View edit history (verify sorted from most recent to oldest)

- Soft delete a todo (verify it doesn't appear in normal list)
- View paginated trash list
- Restore a todo from trash (verify it returns to normal list)
- Permanently delete a todo from trash (verify edit history is also deleted)

- Filter todos: all / complete only / incomplete only
- Sort todos by creation date (newest first, oldest first)
- Sort todos by start date (nulls appear last)
- Sort todos by due date (nulls appear last)

- Verify user isolation: user A cannot see user B's todos, trash, or history

scenario.draft:
Verify that a first-time visitor with a previously unseen device fingerprint creates a new guest identity record, establishes a new guest session, and receives a valid JWT token pair.

Test steps:
1. Send POST /todoApp/auth/guest/join with a unique fingerprint hash (never submitted before), a valid href URL, and a referrer URL
2. Verify HTTP 200 response with ITodoAppGuest.IAuthorized body containing:
   - id: a valid UUID (the newly created guest identity)
   - fingerprint: matches the submitted fingerprint exactly
   - created_at: valid ISO 8601 timestamp
   - updated_at: valid ISO 8601 timestamp equal to created_at (brand new record)
   - token.access: non-empty JWT string
   - token.refresh: non-empty JWT string, different from token.access
   - token.expired_at: future ISO 8601 timestamp (access token expiration)
   - token.refreshable_until: future ISO 8601 timestamp beyond expired_at (refresh window)
3. Send a second join with a different unique fingerprint and confirm a different id is returned, confirming each fingerprint maps to its own guest identity

dependencies.purpose:
Essential authentication prerequisite:
This join operation (post /todoApp/auth/guest/join) must be executed before any operations requiring 'guest' actor authorization.
It establishes the necessary user account and authentication context for the 'guest' actor, enabling subsequent API calls that depend on this specific authorization level.
Without this join operation, the main scenario endpoint and its dependencies will fail due to insufficient authentication credentials.

functions.name: test_api_guest_join_new_identity

scenario.draft:
Verify that a returning visitor with an already-known device fingerprint reuses the same guest identity record, creates a brand new session, and receives a fresh JWT token pair distinct from the previous session.

Test steps:
1. Send first POST /todoApp/auth/guest/join with fingerprint "fp-returning-001", href and referrer — capture the response (id, created_at, tokens)
2. Send second POST /todoApp/auth/guest/join with the same fingerprint "fp-returning-001" (optionally with different href/referrer values)
3. Verify the second response:
   - id: identical to the id from step 1 (guest identity reused, not duplicated)
   - fingerprint: matches "fp-returning-001"
   - created_at: unchanged from step 1 (original creation time preserved)
   - updated_at: more recent than created_at (record was touched on this return visit)
   - token.access: new non-empty JWT string, different from step 1's access token
   - token.refresh: new non-empty JWT string, different from step 1's refresh token
   - token.expired_at: new future timestamp for the second session
   - token.refreshable_until: new future timestamp for the second session
4. Confirm both requests returned 200 independently — identity persists across sessions while each join creates a distinct session with its own token pair

scenario.draft:
Verify that a guest can successfully refresh their session using a valid refresh token obtained from a prior join operation.

Steps:
1. Call POST /todoApp/auth/guest/join to create a guest identity and obtain the initial JWT token pair (access token and refresh token).
2. Call POST /todoApp/auth/guest/refresh with the refresh token from step 1 as the request body.

Expected behavior:
- The refresh call returns HTTP 200 with an ITodoAppGuest.IAuthorized response.
- The response contains a new access token and new refresh token, both distinct from the tokens issued in step 1.
- The access token and refresh token are non-empty strings.
- The expired_at timestamp is a future ISO 8601 datetime.
- The refreshable_until timestamp is a future ISO 8601 datetime and is later than expired_at.
- The id field remains the same guest UUID from the join response (same guest identity persisted across sessions).
- The fingerprint field remains the same as from the join response.
- The created_at timestamp matches the original join timestamp (unchanged).
- The updated_at timestamp reflects the join time (not updated on refresh, only on join).

This scenario validates the core token rotation mechanism — a new session is created while preserving the guest identity.

dependencies.purpose: Create a guest identity and session to obtain a valid refresh token for the refresh operation

functions.name: test_api_guest_session_refresh_success

scenario.draft:
Verify that refreshing with a token from an expired session is rejected with 401, requiring the guest to re-join.

Steps:
1. Call POST /todoApp/auth/guest/join to create a guest identity and session, obtaining the refresh token.
2. Wait until the session's expired_at timestamp has passed (simulate or fast-forward time past the session expiration).
3. Call POST /todoApp/auth/guest/refresh with the now-expired refresh token.

Expected behavior:
- The refresh call returns HTTP 401 Unauthorized.
- The response body contains an error message indicating the session has expired and the guest must re-join.
- No new tokens are issued — the guest identity is not extended.

This scenario validates the session expiry business rule: once a guest session's expired_at timestamp is in the past, token refresh is denied and the guest must call the join endpoint again to establish a new session.

scenario.draft: Test the successful restoration of a soft-deleted todo from the trash back to the active todo list, verifying full data preservation and return to full active functionality. First, authenticate as a member and create a todo with all fields populated (title, description, start date, due date). Optionally, make an edit to the todo to generate edit history. Soft-delete the todo to move it to the trash. Then restore it using the target endpoint and verify: (1) the response returns the full todo with all original fields intact — title, description, start date, due date unchanged, completed_at still null (incomplete), created_at unchanged, and updated_at refreshed to the current timestamp; (2) the deleted_at field is cleared (the todo is no longer in the trash); (3) the todo reappears in the normal active todo list and no longer appears in the trash list; (4) all edit history entries remain fully accessible after restoration. Also verify the restored todo can be subsequently edited and toggled, confirming it has returned to full active functionality.

According to the specification's edge case handling for race conditions and concurrent restores, the second call should succeed idempotently, returning the restored todo rather than producing an error.
